QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_44

question.text: If the 95% one-month VaR of an AIF is INR 2 crore, the correct interpretation is:

answer.text: There is a 95% probability the fund will not lose more than INR 2 crore over the next month
The fund is guaranteed to lose INR 2 crore
The fund's NAV will grow by INR 2 crore
The fund's management fee will be INR 2 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.9.3: 95% one-month VaR of INR 2 crore means 95% probability that fund will NOT lose more than INR 2 crore over the next month. Equivalently, 5% chance of losing > INR 2 crore. The Trap: Option B confuses probability with certainty. Options C and D are unrelated. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Derivatives) covers VaR extensively; XXI-B for PMS. Manager's Pro-Tip: VaR does NOT tell you how much you'd lose in the 5% tail — use Expected Shortfall (CVaR) alongside. SEBI-registered Cat III AIFs using derivatives should stress-test beyond VaR in their risk policy.
